places.name: St. Patrick's Cathedral, New York
places.why: First steps into Catholic practice in a big-city parish anyone can walk into.
places.scene: Wide view of the cathedral's white spires above Fifth Avenue at early morning, doors open, small figures on the steps.
places.realVisit: Open daily on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan; walk in for free and stay for a weekday Mass.

spots.scene: Wide view through the bronze doors at morning, a holy water font catching the light, distant people crossing themselves; no close faces.

places.name: San Fernando Cathedral, San Antonio
places.why: Mexican-American home faith: medals, candles and grace at the family table.

places.realVisit: Downtown San Antonio, Texas; free to enter, and the Missions trail is a short drive south.

places.realVisit: Fly to Tel Aviv, then a bus or tour to Nazareth; the basilica is free and open daily.

places.realVisit: A short walk or taxi east of Jerusalem's Old City; the churches open mornings and afternoons.

spots.scene: Side chapel in warm candle glow, small first-communion children seen from behind at the rail.

spots.name: Altar of St Jerome, tomb of St John XXIII
spots.scene: Quiet altar with flowers and a glass reliquary glow, a few pilgrims kneeling far off at noon.

spots.scene: Wide view of the parish church on the broad avenue to St Peter's on a Sunday morning, doors open and a congregation filing in, the great dome ahead; no close faces.

spots.scene: Low vaulted grotto with a simple tomb slab and one candle, cool morning stillness.

spots.scene: Wide square in late afternoon, a small marble marker in the cobbles, pigeons, distant crowd.

spots.scene: The palace façade at Sunday noon, one window open, a crowd below seen from far behind.

spots.scene: A plain stone tomb in the grottoes, white flowers, soft evening light.

spots.scene: A small monastery among the trees of the Vatican Gardens at quiet morning, dome behind.

spots.scene: The simple guesthouse beside the basilica at early dawn, one lit window.

spots.scene: The bronze Holy Door standing open, a line of pilgrims entering seen from behind, morning.

spots.scene: The empty rain-wet square at dusk, one small white figure far away under a canopy, a crucifix and a monstrance glow.

spots.scene: The loggia draped in red at evening, white smoke drifting overhead, a huge crowd waving below.

spots.scene: Wide view of the small ancient church of the martyrs Nereus and Achilleus among umbrella pines at late afternoon, the ruined baths looming behind and its painted walls lined with martyr scenes inside; no close faces.

spots.scene: Great tapestries of new saints hanging from the façade on a bright Sunday morning.

spots.name: Chapel of St Sebastian, tomb of St John Paul II
spots.scene: A side chapel with a white marble slab and candles, pilgrims kneeling far back.

spots.name: Piazza dei Protomartiri Romani
spots.scene: A small paved square beside the basilica where Nero's circus stood, cool shadow at dawn.

spots.name: Altar of St Joseph, tomb of Sts Simon and Jude
spots.scene: The left transept altar in afternoon light, an old mosaic above, quiet.

spots.name: Altar of St Basil, relics of St Josaphat
spots.scene: A marble altar with a glass reliquary glow, Eastern-rite pilgrims seen from behind.

spots.name: Vatican Radio tower in the Vatican Gardens
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Vatican Radio tower in the Vatican Gardens at afternoon: a round stone tower with antennas rising above green gardens; no close faces.

spots.name: Casina Pio IV, Pontifical Academy of Sciences
spots.scene: Wide view of the decorated garden villa of Pius IV in the Vatican Gardens at afternoon, fountains still, no close faces.

spots.name: Interior drum walkway of Michelangelo's dome
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Interior drum walkway of Michelangelo's dome at midday: the ring gallery high inside the dome, the basilica floor tiny below; no close faces.

spots.name: Vatican Apostolic Archive, Cortile del Belvedere
spots.scene: Wide view of the long Belvedere courtyard at afternoon, the archive's entrance quiet under the walls, no close faces.

spots.name: Chapel of the Blessed Sacrament, St. Peter's
spots.scene: Wide view into a gilded chapel behind wrought-iron gates at early morning, a gold tabernacle glowing, no close faces.

spots.name: Choir Chapel of the Canons, St. Peter's
spots.scene: Wide view of carved choir stalls and an open Gospel book on a lectern at evening Vespers, no close faces.

spots.name: Baptistery chapel of St. Peter's
spots.scene: A porphyry font in a side chapel at afternoon.

spots.name: Gregorian Chapel, St. Peter's
spots.scene: Wide view of a marble chapel under a small dome at Sunday morning Mass, distant congregation standing, no close faces.

spots.name: Via della Conciliazione toward the basilica
spots.scene: Wide view down a long avenue toward the great dome at dusk, crowds of many nations walking together, no close faces.

places.name: Sistine Chapel
places.why: Year two opens the whole library of Scripture, and Michelangelo painted its first pages overhead.
places.scene: The Sistine Chapel at mid-morning, wide from the entrance, the ceiling of creation glowing above a quiet hall.
places.realVisit: Book the Vatican Museums online; the chapel is at the end of the route, silence asked inside.

spots.name: Moses and Christ fresco cycles on the side walls
spots.scene: Two painted walls of stories face each other across the chapel in soft morning light, a library made of pictures.

spots.name: Separation of Light from Darkness panel
spots.scene: Wide upward view of the ceiling's first panel, swirling light pulling away from dark, God shown only as light.

spots.name: Creation of the Sun, Moon and Plants panel
spots.scene: The ceiling vault at noon with the panel of sun and moon, painted heavens crowded with color.

spots.name: Creation of Adam panel
spots.scene: Two reaching hands under the vault seen from far below, the gap between them lit gold.

spots.name: Cosmatesque marble floor of the chapel
spots.scene: The inlaid stone floor in long afternoon light, dust in the air, the painted ceiling a blur above.

spots.name: Creation of Eve at the centre of the vault
spots.scene: Wide view up into the Sistine vault in soft morning light, the central panel of Eve rising from the sleeping Adam seen far overhead, visitors small below, no close faces, God shown only as light.

spots.name: Borgia Apartments
spots.scene: Richly painted rooms in lamplight, empty.

spots.name: Ceiling vault from the marble screen, Sistine Chapel
spots.scene: Wide view up the length of the painted vault from the marble screen in hushed morning light, light falling from the high windows, no faces shown.

spots.name: Sistine Chapel beneath the Last Judgment, conclave
spots.scene: Rows of draped tables beneath the great wall, red robes from behind, a stove pipe.

spots.name: Michelangelo's Jonah above the altar
spots.scene: Wide view up the altar wall to the leaning prophet of mercy on the vault, figures tiny below.

spots.name: Sistine Chapel choir loft (cantoria)
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Sistine Chapel choir loft (cantoria) at quiet early hour: the small marble singers' balcony looking across the empty chapel to the great altar wall; no close faces.

spots.name: Last Judgment altar wall
spots.scene: The whole altar wall seen from the far end of the chapel at dusk, swirling figures too distant for faces.

spots.name: Vatican Gardens below the Sistine Chapel roof
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Vatican Gardens below the Sistine Chapel roof at spring morning: fountains and green terraces with the plain brick bulk of the chapel rising behind; no close faces.

spots.name: Perugino wall frescoes, Sistine Chapel
spots.scene: A wide view along the side wall's fresco band, a painted piazza and temple in calm daylight.

places.name: Al-Qurna, Garden of Eden tradition
places.why: Where the Tigris meets the Euphrates, an old tradition places the garden, the fall and the first promise.
places.scene: The meeting of two great rivers at dusk, palms and reeds, a wide flat land under a huge sky.
places.realVisit: Al-Qurna lies north of Basra by road; the riverside Adam's Tree park is open to visitors.

spots.name: Adam's Tree park
spots.scene: An old dry tree in a small walled park beside the river, golden evening light, no people close.

spots.name: Confluence of the Tigris and Euphrates
spots.scene: Two rivers merging under a pale dawn, reeds rustling, a single small boat far off.

spots.name: Tigris corniche at Qurna
spots.scene: The riverfront at first light, a thin gold line on the water like a promise.

spots.name: East bank of the Shatt al-Arab
spots.scene: An empty riverbank east of the confluence at dusk, one distant walker heading away.

places.name: Mount Ararat and the Doğubayazıt plain
places.why: The mountain where Genesis says the ark came to rest.
places.scene: Snow-capped Ararat rising over a green plain after rain, a rainbow over the slopes.
places.realVisit: Fly to Ağrı or drive from Doğubayazıt; viewpoints are reachable by road year-round.

spots.name: Durupınar ship-shaped formation
spots.scene: A boat-shaped ridge in the hills at morning, Ararat white on the horizon, clouds gathering.

spots.name: Ishak Pasha Palace terrace facing Ararat
spots.scene: The palace terrace after a storm, a full rainbow arching toward the mountain.

places.name: Ziggurat of Ur
places.why: Abraham set out from Ur of the Chaldees; its stepped tower recalls Babel.
places.scene: The great stepped ziggurat of Ur in desert evening light, long shadows across the sand.
places.realVisit: Ur is near Nasiriyah in southern Iraq; local guides lead visits to the ziggurat.

spots.name: Great Ziggurat of Ur
spots.scene: The ziggurat's staircase climbing into a hazy sky, tiny figures at the base for scale.

spots.name: Restored dwelling known as Abraham's House
spots.scene: Mud-brick courtyard walls at sunrise, a road leading out into open desert.

places.name: Mamre (Ramat al-Khalil), Hebron
places.why: Abraham pitched his tent by the oaks of Mamre: covenant, visitors, bargaining, promise.
places.scene: Terraced Hebron hills at evening, old stone walls and olive trees, tents of a camp far off.
places.realVisit: Hebron is reached from Jerusalem with a licensed guide; Ramat al-Khalil is on the city's north edge.

spots.name: Vineyards of Beit Ummar
spots.scene: Grape terraces on the hills at sunset, a road below where a weary band returns home.

spots.name: Herodian enclosure at Ramat al-Khalil
spots.scene: Great ancient stones under a sky thick with stars, one small figure gazing up.

spots.name: Abraham's Well at Ramat al-Khalil
spots.scene: A stone-lined well in the midday heat, a lone figure resting in thin shade.

spots.name: Oak of Abraham, Holy Trinity Monastery grounds
spots.scene: An ancient propped-up oak in a monastery garden at noon, a table set in its shade.

spots.name: Bani Na'im ridge toward the Dead Sea
spots.scene: A ridge looking down toward a hazy Dead Sea basin at dusk, two small figures talking.

spots.name: Valley of Eshcol vineyards
spots.scene: Heavy grape clusters on low vines in early morning, the valley opening south.

places.name: Tel Be'er Sheva
places.why: Abraham and Isaac lived at Beersheba: laughter, the binding journey, wells, and two brothers.
places.scene: An ancient mound in the northern Negev at golden hour, desert stretching in every direction.
places.realVisit: Tel Be'er Sheva National Park sits just east of the city of Beersheba, open daily.

spots.name: City gate of Tel Be'er Sheva
spots.scene: The old city gate at warm morning light, a courtyard where a family might have laughed.

spots.name: Abraham's Well, old Beersheba
spots.scene: A stone well under a tamarisk at dawn, a donkey and a long road north into the hills.

spots.name: Great well of Tel Be'er Sheva
spots.scene: A deep ancient well shaft at late afternoon, camels resting in the distance.

spots.name: Tents by Nahal Be'er Sheva
spots.scene: Low Bedouin tents along a dry streambed at dusk, smoke from a cooking fire.

spots.name: Storehouses of Tel Be'er Sheva
spots.scene: Rows of pillared storerooms at twilight, a dim lamp glowing in one doorway.

places.name: Beitin (Bethel)
places.why: Jacob dreamed of the ladder at Bethel, then loved Rachel, who lies on the Bethlehem road.
places.scene: Rocky hills north of Jerusalem at night, stones scattered on a ridge under deep stars.
places.realVisit: Beitin is a village north of Ramallah; Rachel's Tomb is on the Bethlehem road, both with a local guide.

spots.name: Burj Beitin ridge
spots.scene: A stony ridge under a starry night, a shaft of light rising from the ground to the sky.

spots.name: Rachel's Tomb
spots.scene: The domed tomb at dusk seen from the road, a single lamp in its window.

places.name: Jabbok River at Penuel
places.why: Jacob wrestled till daybreak by the Jabbok, and later Balaam's story was found carved nearby.
places.scene: A green river valley cutting through brown Jordanian hills at first light.
places.realVisit: The Zarqa valley is an hour north of Amman by car; Tell Deir Alla is beside the main valley road.

spots.name: Tulul adh-Dhahab twin hills
spots.scene: Two hills above the river at the very first gray light, the sky just turning pink.

spots.name: Ford of the Jabbok (Zarqa) River
spots.scene: Shallow water over stones at sunrise, a far line of travellers and herds on the other side.

spots.name: Tell Deir Alla (Balaam inscription site)
spots.scene: A low mound by a dusty road at noon, a donkey stopped dead on the path.

places.name: Nablus (Shechem) and the Samarian hills
places.why: Between Mount Ebal and Gerizim lie Joseph's wells and tomb, Jacob's Well, and the road the lepers walked.
places.scene: Two mountains framing a valley city at morning, olive terraces climbing the slopes.
places.realVisit: Nablus is reached from Jerusalem with a licensed guide; Jacob's Well church is open to pilgrims.

spots.name: Joseph's Tomb, Nablus
spots.scene: A small domed tomb in the valley at morning, wide fields where the brothers grazed flocks.

spots.name: Tel Dothan
spots.scene: A grassy mound above a plain at noon, a dry cistern in the foreground, a caravan far off.

spots.name: Tel Balata (ancient Shechem)
spots.scene: Massive ancient gate stones at sunset, a great standing stone in a temple courtyard.

spots.name: Sanur hill fortress (Bethulia tradition)
spots.scene: A hilltop fortress over a plain at night, distant campfires of an army below.

spots.name: Church of St George, Burqin
spots.scene: An ancient stone church in a hillside village at morning, a road winding out to the fields.

spots.name: Ain al-Far'a spring (Aenon tradition)
spots.scene: A spring pooling among rocks in a green wadi, morning light on clear water.

spots.name: Mount Gerizim summit
spots.scene: Wide view from the summit of Mount Gerizim at noon, the ancient sanctuary ruins in the foreground and Nablus filling the valley below Mount Ebal; no close faces.

spots.name: Fields of Askar below Mount Ebal
spots.scene: Golden wheat ready for harvest at noon, the mountain behind, a path through the fields.

places.name: Memphis (Mit Rahina)
places.why: Joseph rose from prisoner to ruler in Pharaoh's Egypt, whose old capital was Memphis.
places.scene: Palm groves and ancient ruins beside the Nile valley at golden hour, pyramids on the horizon.
places.realVisit: Memphis and Saqqara are a short drive south of Cairo, usually visited together with Giza.

spots.name: Temple of Ptah ruins, Mit Rahina
spots.scene: Fallen temple blocks among palms in shadowy late light, a barred doorway in the stone.

spots.name: Step Pyramid of Djoser, Saqqara
spots.scene: The stepped pyramid at dawn against a pink sky, desert empty around it.

spots.name: Pyramids of Giza (Joseph's granaries legend)
spots.scene: The three pyramids at sunset seen from the desert, camels walking a far ridge.

spots.name: Colossus of Ramesses II, Mit Rahina
spots.scene: A giant fallen statue under a hall roof, shafts of light, a few distant visitors.

spots.name: Nile bank at Badrashin
spots.scene: The Nile at sunset with feluccas, wheat fields running down to the water.

places.name: Old Cairo (Fustat)
places.why: Hebrew midwives defied Pharaoh, and tradition places the basket in the reeds here.
places.scene: Old Cairo's domes and walls by the Nile at morning, palm tops above old brick lanes.
places.realVisit: Coptic Cairo is a stop on the Cairo metro (Mar Girgis); the synagogue and pottery village are walkable.

spots.name: Fustat pottery village
spots.scene: Mud-brick kilns smoking at dawn, rows of drying clay pots, workers far in the distance.

spots.name: Ben Ezra Synagogue garden
spots.scene: A quiet garden by an old synagogue at morning, reeds and water nearby, a woven basket by the path.

places.name: Mount Sinai and St. Catherine's Monastery (second visit)
places.why: Moses met God at the burning bush and received the Law on Sinai; Elijah heard the still small voice here.
places.scene: The granite peaks of Sinai at dawn, a walled monastery in the valley below.
places.realVisit: St Catherine's is reached from Sharm el-Sheikh; climb Jebel Musa before dawn with a Bedouin guide.

spots.name: Wadi el-Leja and the Monastery of the Forty Martyrs
spots.scene: Wide view of the remote valley of el-Leja at dawn, a small walled monastery among olive trees beneath the red granite flank of Sinai; no close faces.

spots.name: Well of Moses, St Catherine's Monastery
spots.scene: A stone well in the monastery courtyard at morning, a shepherd's staff leaning on it.

spots.name: Ras Safsafa peak above the plain
spots.scene: Wide view from the Ras Safsafa peak at stormy dusk, thunderheads over the granite ridges and the plain far below, tiny pilgrims on the path, no close faces, God only as light breaking through cloud.

spots.name: Steps of Repentance
spots.scene: Thousands of rough granite steps climbing a ravine in early morning shadow.

spots.name: Plain of er-Raha
spots.scene: A wide desert plain at the mountain's foot under noon haze, tents far off.

spots.name: Cleft below the summit (Moses' Cave)
spots.scene: A dark cleft in the rock, a bright light passing just beyond the opening.

spots.name: Elijah's Basin (Farsh Elias)
spots.scene: A hollow with a lone cypress and a tiny chapel at evening, the wind dropping to silence.

places.name: Tanis (San el-Hagar)
places.why: The Delta cities of Pharaoh are where the plagues and the first Passover are set.
places.scene: Ruins of a great temple scattered across a brown mound in the Nile Delta, evening haze.
places.realVisit: Tanis lies in the eastern Delta, about three hours' drive northeast of Cairo.

spots.name: Temple of Amun ruins, Tanis
spots.scene: Toppled obelisks and statues on a dusty mound under a heavy, darkening sky.

spots.name: Qantir fields (Pi-Ramesses)
spots.scene: Flat green fields at night under a full moon, lamplight in low houses, doorways marked.

places.name: Ayun Musa (Springs of Moses)
places.why: On the eastern shore of the Gulf of Suez, tradition remembers the crossing and Miriam's song.
places.scene: Palm-ringed springs near a wide sea shore at sunrise, desert mountains beyond.
places.realVisit: Ayun Musa is a short drive south of the Suez tunnel on the Sinai coast road.

spots.name: Gulf of Suez shore below Ayun Musa
spots.scene: A wide sea at dawn with a strong wind, the far shore a dark line, a crowd small on the beach.

spots.name: Springs of Moses palm grove
spots.scene: Palms around desert springs at morning, a circle of distant dancers with tambourines.

places.name: Wadi Feiran oasis
places.why: The largest oasis of Sinai, long linked with manna and the battle at Rephidim.
places.scene: A long green oasis of palms and tamarisks in a red granite valley at morning.
places.realVisit: Wadi Feiran is on the road to St Catherine's; Bedouin guides lead walks into the oasis.

spots.name: Tamarisk groves of Wadi Feiran
spots.scene: Tamarisk branches glistening with white morning dew on the ground, baskets left by the trees.

spots.name: Jebel Tahuna above the oasis
spots.scene: A small hilltop above the valley at sunset, a distant figure with both arms raised.

places.name: Timna Park
places.why: A life-size model of the desert Tabernacle stands in Timna, where wilderness laws come alive.
places.scene: Red sandstone cliffs and desert valley at golden hour, a tent sanctuary in the plain.
places.realVisit: Timna Park is 25 km north of Eilat on Route 90, open daily.

spots.name: Life-size Tabernacle model
spots.scene: A woven tent sanctuary in a fenced courtyard at morning, light glowing from within.

spots.name: Solomon's Pillars
spots.scene: Huge red rock columns at sunset, the valley floor in shadow below.

spots.name: Timna Lake
spots.scene: A calm desert lake with palms at dawn, open land waiting to rest.

spots.name: Mushroom rock formation
spots.scene: A mushroom-shaped rock under a soft evening glow, hands raised in blessing far off.

places.name: Mount Nebo
places.why: Moses gave his last teaching on the plains of Moab and saw the promised land from Nebo.
places.scene: The view west from Mount Nebo at evening, the Jordan valley and Dead Sea in haze.
places.realVisit: Mount Nebo is 40 minutes from Amman via Madaba; the Franciscan memorial church is open daily.

spots.name: Plains of Moab near Shuneh
spots.scene: A great camp spread across a plain at dawn, mountains to the east, the river beyond.

spots.name: Moses Memorial Church
spots.scene: A stone church on a hilltop at noon, two paths going down the slope, one toward green.

spots.name: Brazen Serpent monument lookout
spots.scene: A metal serpent-cross sculpture on the summit at sunset, the promised land glowing below.

spots.name: Tall el-Hammam (Abel-Shittim), the spies' starting camp
spots.scene: Wide view over the excavated mound of Tall el-Hammam at late afternoon, the Jordan valley and the green smudge of Jericho across the river, no close faces.

places.name: Basilica of the Transfiguration, Mount Tabor
places.why: Deborah's army gathered on Tabor; Jesus raised a widow's son at Nain below and was transfigured on the summit.
places.scene: The dome-shaped mountain rising alone from the Jezreel Valley at dawn.
places.realVisit: Taxis climb the switchback road to the summit basilica from Dabburiya; the views are best at sunrise.

spots.name: Summit lookout over the Jezreel Valley
spots.scene: A wide valley seen from the summit at morning, a lone palm and an army gathering below.

spots.name: Spring of Harod (Ein Harod)
spots.scene: A spring at the foot of Gilboa at evening, soldiers small kneeling to drink.

spots.name: Nain (Nein) village and its chapel
spots.scene: A small village chapel at the foot of a hill, a funeral procession stopped on the road.

spots.name: Basilica of the Transfiguration nave
spots.scene: The basilica on the summit at dawn, golden light pouring through the clouds overhead.

spots.name: Greek Orthodox Monastery of Elijah, Mount Tabor
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Greek Orthodox Monastery of Elijah, Mount Tabor at misty dawn: a domed monastery among pines on the summit ridge; no close faces.

places.name: Valley of Elah
places.why: The Shephelah valleys of Samson and of David's stand against Goliath.
places.scene: A broad valley of fields between low hills at morning, a stream bed winding through.
places.realVisit: The Valley of Elah is 30 minutes southwest of Jerusalem; Khirbet Qeiyafa has a marked trail.

spots.name: Tel Tzora (Samson's Zorah)
spots.scene: A hill above the Sorek valley at dusk, wheat fields and foxes in the stubble.

spots.name: Elah brook (Wadi es-Sunt)
spots.scene: A dry streambed of smooth stones at morning, two armies tiny on opposite hills.

spots.name: Khirbet Qeiyafa fortress
spots.scene: A hilltop fortress gate at sunset, two figures parting at a distance.

places.name: Shepherds' fields of Beit Sahour
places.why: Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields and David kept sheep here before he was anointed.
places.scene: Terraced fields and shepherds' caves east of Bethlehem at golden hour.
places.realVisit: Beit Sahour is next to Bethlehem; the Shepherds' Field sites are a short taxi ride from Manger Square.

spots.name: Greek Orthodox Shepherds' Field
spots.scene: Two women walking toward Bethlehem across stony fields at evening.

spots.name: Barley terraces below Beit Sahour
spots.scene: Barley harvest at midday, a woman gleaning behind reapers, sheaves stacked.

spots.name: King David's Wells, Bethlehem
spots.scene: Ancient cisterns in a hillside garden at morning, a flask of oil glinting.

spots.name: Shepherds' caves, Catholic Shepherds' Field
spots.scene: A cave sheepfold opening onto a hillside at dusk, a shepherd far off at the gate.

places.name: Tel Shiloh
places.why: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, where Hannah prayed and Samuel heard his name.
places.scene: A terraced hilltop among olive groves at evening, the ruins of an ancient town.
places.realVisit: Tel Shiloh is north of Jerusalem off Route 60, with a visitor centre and film.

spots.name: Tabernacle platform, Tel Shiloh
spots.scene: A flat rock terrace on the hilltop at dusk, a woman praying alone, lips moving.

spots.name: Byzantine church mosaics, Shiloh
spots.scene: A mosaic floor under a protective roof at night, one small lamp still burning.

spots.name: Tell el-Ful (Gibeah of Saul)
spots.scene: An unfinished palace on a hilltop at noon, a tall young man far off among donkeys.

places.name: En Gedi
places.why: David hid in the caves of En Gedi; the oasis is a fitting place for the Bible's wisdom.
places.scene: A desert oasis of waterfalls and caves above the Dead Sea at morning.
places.realVisit: En Gedi Nature Reserve is on Route 90 beside the Dead Sea, open daily.

spots.name: Dodim Cave above Nahal David
spots.scene: Wide view of a cave mouth in the pale cliffs above Nahal David in harsh noon light, ibex on the ledges and the Dead Sea shimmering below; no close faces.

spots.name: Chalcolithic temple, En Gedi
spots.scene: An ancient stone enclosure on a terrace at sunrise, the sea below changing color.

spots.name: Ancient synagogue of En Gedi
spots.scene: A mosaic floor among palms in late afternoon, inscriptions catching the light.

places.name: City of David, Jerusalem
places.why: David's city, Solomon's Temple hill, Isaiah's and Hezekiah's Jerusalem, and the Pool of Siloam.
places.scene: The narrow ridge south of the Old City walls at morning, excavations and the Kidron Valley below.
places.realVisit: The City of David park is just outside the Dung Gate; the water tunnel walk needs sandals and a torch.

spots.name: Stepped Stone Structure
spots.scene: A great stepped stone ramp at morning, a joyful crowd small at its top.

spots.name: Large Stone Structure (David's palace)
spots.scene: Palace foundations at dusk, a rooftop view toward lit houses below.

spots.name: Absalom's Pillar, Kidron Valley
spots.scene: A tall rock-cut tomb in the valley at sunset, a lone mourner far away.

spots.name: Pool of Gibeon, el-Jib
spots.scene: A great rock-cut pool with a spiral stair at night under a quiet moon.

spots.name: Givati excavation lookout toward the Temple Mount
spots.scene: The Temple Mount walls seen across excavations at dawn, sunlight on old stone.

spots.name: Hezekiah's Broad Wall, Jewish Quarter
spots.scene: A massive ancient wall in a sunken plaza, smoke-like light filling the air above.

spots.name: Gihon Spring
spots.scene: Water flowing in a dim rock chamber, a shaft of light from above.

spots.name: Pool of Siloam steps
spots.scene: Broad stone steps down into a pool at festival morning, water poured from a jar.

spots.name: Pilgrimage Road (Herodian stepped street)
spots.scene: An underground stone street lit by lamps, tall golden lampstands imagined at its end.

spots.name: Siloam Tunnel exit
spots.scene: A tunnel mouth opening into bright daylight, water rushing out.

spots.name: Byzantine Shiloah pool
spots.scene: A small pool under a fig tree at noon, a man walking away seeing everything new.

places.name: Mount Carmel, Stella Maris
places.why: Elijah's mountain, home of the Carmelites, where fire fell on the sacrifice.
places.scene: Carmel's ridge above the Mediterranean at sunset, a monastery on the headland.
places.realVisit: Stella Maris is on Haifa's Carmel ridge, reachable by cable car; Muhraqa is a short drive southeast.

spots.name: Elijah's Cave, Haifa
spots.scene: A cave entrance on the hillside at evening, a small jar and lamp inside.

spots.name: Muhraqa, Carmelite Monastery of the Sacrifice
spots.scene: A ridge-top altar at noon, a column of fire falling as light, the Jezreel plain below.

places.name: Baptism site on the Jordan (Qasr al-Yahud) (second visit)
places.why: At the Jordan, Elijah was taken up, Naaman was healed, and John baptized Jesus.
places.scene: The slow brown Jordan between reeds and tamarisks at dawn, churches on both banks.
places.realVisit: Qasr al-Yahud (west bank) and Al-Maghtas (Jordan) are both open to visitors; dress modestly.

spots.name: Elijah's Hill (Tell Mar Elias)
spots.scene: A small hill above the river at dusk, a whirl of fiery light rising toward the sky.

spots.name: Deir Hajla, Monastery of St Gerasimos near the Jordan
spots.scene: Wide view of the walled desert monastery of Deir Hajla at midday, palms and a green garden against bare plain, the Jordan's thicket a few kilometres east; no close faces.

spots.name: Church of St John the Baptist, Al-Maghtas
spots.scene: A golden-domed church above the river at morning, crowds coming down to the water.

spots.name: Bethany beyond the Jordan baptism pools
spots.scene: Ancient stone pools among reeds at afternoon, two figures following a distant walker.

spots.name: Reed-lined Jordan bend
spots.scene: The river at dawn, the sky opening with light and a dove-shaped glow over the water.

places.name: Babylon and the Hillah plain (second visit)
places.why: The exile, Ezekiel's vision, the three young men and the fall of Babylon all belong to this plain.
places.scene: The Euphrates plain at dusk, palm groves and the reconstructed walls of Babylon.
places.realVisit: Babylon is near Hillah, about two hours south of Baghdad; al-Kifl is a short drive further.

spots.name: Ishtar Gate replica, Babylon
spots.scene: A blue-glazed gate at evening, a long line of exiles walking in.

spots.name: Ezekiel's shrine, al-Kifl
spots.scene: A conical shrine roof above a dry plain at dawn, wind stirring the dust.

spots.name: Processional Way of Babylon
spots.scene: A brick avenue between high walls at night, the glow of a great furnace far off.

spots.name: Lion of Babylon statue
spots.scene: An ancient stone lion among ruins at sunset, empty walls behind it.

places.name: St. Patrick's Cathedral, New York (second visit)
places.why: New York carries Isaiah's peace on the UN's walls, Dorothy Day's houses of hospitality, and St Patrick's.
places.scene: Midtown Manhattan at evening, the white spires of St Patrick's between towers.
places.realVisit: All these spots are walkable in Manhattan; St Patrick's is open daily on Fifth Avenue.

spots.name: Swords into Plowshares statue, UN garden
spots.scene: A bronze figure beating a sword in a riverside garden at morning, the UN tower behind.

spots.name: Isaiah Wall, Ralph Bunche Park
spots.scene: Carved words on a granite wall above steps at golden hour, trees in leaf.

spots.name: St Joseph House (Catholic Worker)
spots.scene: A plain brick house on the Lower East Side at evening, a door open to strangers.

spots.name: Maryhouse (Catholic Worker)
spots.scene: An old brick building on a quiet street at morning, sunlight on the front steps.

spots.name: Church of the Nativity, Second Avenue
spots.scene: A small parish church at dusk, people far off carrying bags of food.

spots.name: St Patrick's Cathedral nave
spots.scene: The great Gothic nave in afternoon light, a few figures kneeling far away.

spots.name: Fifth Avenue parade route at St Patrick's
spots.scene: Green banners and bagpipers far down the avenue in March sun, the cathedral spires above.

places.name: Fishamble Street, Dublin
places.why: Handel's Messiah, which made Isaiah's comfort and suffering servant famous, premiered here.
places.scene: Old Dublin by the Liffey at dusk, a cathedral tower above a narrow street.
places.realVisit: Fishamble Street is beside Christ Church Cathedral in central Dublin; Messiah is sung there each April.

spots.name: Fishamble Street (Messiah premiere site)
spots.scene: A narrow street at evening, warm windows, choir music spilling out.

spots.name: Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin
spots.scene: Cathedral stones under a gray sky, a single shaft of light inside the nave.

places.name: Jerusalem of Jeremiah
places.why: Jeremiah was born at Anathoth and wept over Jerusalem's fall.
places.scene: Jerusalem's walls and valleys at dawn, the hills of Anathoth to the northeast.
places.realVisit: All spots are in or near the Old City; Anata is a short drive northeast.

spots.name: Almond terraces of Anata (Anathoth)
spots.scene: A single almond tree in white blossom on a terrace at early spring morning.

spots.name: Akeldama, Hinnom Valley
spots.scene: A valley slope of old tombs at noon, a potter's wheel and shards in the foreground.

spots.name: Western Wall Plaza at dawn
spots.scene: Huge stones at first light, small notes folded into the cracks, figures far apart.

spots.name: Zedekiah's Cave (Solomon's Quarries)
spots.scene: A vast dim quarry beneath the city, one beam of light falling on the floor.

places.name: Tekoa wilderness
places.why: The herdsman-prophet Amos came from Tekoa, at the edge of the wilderness where prophets spoke.
places.scene: Bare hills falling toward the Judean wilderness at morning, shepherds' flocks.
places.realVisit: Tekoa and Herodium are southeast of Bethlehem; Herodium National Park is open daily.

spots.name: Herodium hilltop over the wilderness
spots.scene: A cone-shaped hill at sunrise, empty wilderness rolling east, tender light.

spots.name: Khirbet Tequ'a (Amos's Tekoa)
spots.scene: Stony ruins above a dry wadi at noon, a flash flood rushing far below.

spots.name: Tel Goded (Moresheth-Gath)
spots.scene: A quiet tel among farm fields at evening, a lone walker on the path.

places.name: Old Jaffa (second visit)
places.why: Jonah sailed from Joppa, and Peter raised Tabitha here.
places.scene: Old Jaffa's stone hill and harbour at sunset, the Mediterranean shining.
places.realVisit: Old Jaffa is at the south end of Tel Aviv's beach promenade, walkable from the city.

spots.name: Old Jaffa port
spots.scene: A small harbour at stormy dusk, a ship leaving into gray waves.

spots.name: Suspended Orange Tree, Old Jaffa
spots.scene: A small tree hanging in mid-air over a stone alley at hot noon.

spots.name: Russian Church of St Peter and Tabitha's tomb, Abu Kabir
spots.scene: Wide view of the Russian church's tall bell tower among garden trees in morning light, a quiet path toward the burial cave, no close faces.

places.name: Wadi Rum
places.why: In the immense desert of Edom, Job's questions and God's whirlwind find their scale.
places.scene: Red sand valleys between towering sandstone mountains at sunset.
places.realVisit: Wadi Rum is four hours south of Amman; Bedouin camps offer jeep tours and nights under the stars.

spots.name: Rum valley floor below Jebel Rum
spots.scene: A lone figure sitting in a vast red valley at dusk, ash-gray sky.

spots.name: Khazali Canyon
spots.scene: A narrow canyon in a roaring sandstorm, light whirling at the opening.

places.name: Alexandria
places.why: The Greek Old Testament with its seven extra books, and the Book of Wisdom, came from Alexandria.
places.scene: Alexandria's curved seafront at morning, white buildings and blue water.
places.realVisit: Alexandria is a 2.5-hour train ride from Cairo; the Bibliotheca and Qaitbay are on the Corniche.

spots.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina reading hall
spots.scene: A vast terraced reading hall flooded with sunlight from the slanted roof.

spots.name: Qaitbay Citadel (Pharos site)
spots.scene: A fortress on the harbour point at sunset, calm sea, gulls overhead.

places.name: Hamadan (ancient Ecbatana)
places.why: Tobias and the angel Raphael journeyed to Ecbatana, today's Hamadan.
places.scene: A city beneath snow-topped Mount Alvand at morning, poplar trees lining roads.
places.realVisit: Hamadan is a five-hour drive or short flight from Tehran.

spots.name: Ganjnameh road on Mount Alvand
spots.scene: A mountain road by a waterfall at morning, a young man, a dog and a companion walking.

spots.name: Hegmataneh hill (ancient Ecbatana)
spots.scene: Ancient ruins on a hill at night, one lit window and a quiet garden.

places.name: Catacombs of St. Callixtus, Rome
places.why: The early Christians buried and prayed for their dead in these catacombs.
places.scene: Cypress trees and the Appian Way at evening, the catacomb entrance among the fields.
places.realVisit: The Catacombs of St Callixtus are on the Appian Way in Rome, visited by guided tour.

spots.name: Crypt of the Popes
spots.scene: An underground chamber of carved niches lit by lamps, painted names on the walls.

spots.name: Appian Way beside the catacombs
spots.scene: Old Roman paving stones between cypresses at dusk on All Souls, small candles along the wall.

spots.name: Crypts of Lucina, fish and bread fresco
spots.scene: Tunnel lit by one lamp, a faded fresco of a fish and a basket of bread on the wall.

spots.name: Cubicles of the Sacraments
spots.scene: Small painted burial rooms by lamplight, faded scenes of a font and a shared meal.

spots.name: Crypt of St Cornelius with Cyprian fresco
spots.scene: Lamplit crypt with faded Byzantine-style figures of two bishops seen from afar.

spots.name: San Callisto in Trastevere, well of his martyrdom
spots.scene: Wide view of the small church of San Callisto in its Trastevere square at dusk, ochre walls and lamplight, no figures close.

places.name: Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore (second visit)
places.why: Rome's great basilica of Mary, with the Luke icon, the Christmas crib and the calendar's meridian nearby.
places.scene: Santa Maria Maggiore's bell tower over the Esquiline at morning.
places.realVisit: Santa Maria Maggiore is a short walk from Rome Termini station; the other spots are walkable.

spots.name: Arnolfo di Cambio's Nativity, Sixtine Chapel of Santa Maria Maggiore
spots.scene: Wide view into the domed side chapel in warm evening light, the carved medieval nativity group small and still beneath the gilded dome, no close faces.

spots.name: Meridian line, Santa Maria degli Angeli
spots.scene: A brass line across a marble floor with a spot of sunlight crossing it at noon.

spots.name: Nave mosaics of Santa Maria Maggiore
spots.scene: Gold mosaics glinting along the high nave in early evening, a long wait in the quiet.

spots.name: Crypt of the Holy Crib (Sacra Culla)
spots.scene: A crystal reliquary under the high altar lit softly in the dark.

spots.name: Column of the Immaculate Conception, Piazza Mignanelli
spots.scene: A tall column with a distant Marian statue at dusk on 8 December, flowers heaped at the base.

spots.name: Pantheon (Santa Maria ad Martyres)
spots.scene: The great dome's open eye pouring a beam of light into the round hall.

places.name: Southern Steps of the Temple Mount (second visit)
places.why: The Temple's great southern stairs, where Zechariah served, Simeon waited and the apostles preached.
places.scene: The huge Herodian stairs and walls south of the Temple Mount at morning.
places.realVisit: The Southern Steps are inside the Davidson Center archaeological park by the Dung Gate.

spots.name: Triple Gate (Huldah Gates)
spots.scene: Sealed ancient gates in the high wall at dawn, incense-like haze over the stairs.

spots.name: Herodian staircase of the Southern Steps
spots.scene: Broad stairs at morning, an old man and woman small at the top holding a bundle.

spots.name: The Burnt House, Jewish Quarter
spots.scene: Wide view down into the excavated basement rooms of the Burnt House in dim light, scorched stones and pottery from the year 70, no people, no faces.

spots.name: Wohl Archaeological Museum, Herodian Quarter
spots.scene: Wide view of the excavated priestly mansions beneath the Jewish Quarter in cool lamplight, mosaic floors and stone basins stretching into the shadows; no close faces.

spots.name: Wilson's Arch prayer hall
spots.scene: Wide view under the great stone arch at the north end of the Western Wall in lamp-lit evening, the huge Herodian courses rising into shadow, a few distant figures, no close faces.

spots.name: Double Gate, Southern Wall
spots.scene: A gate at the top of the stairs at three in the afternoon, a beggar's mat left behind.

places.name: Basilica of the Annunciation, Nazareth (second visit)
places.why: Mary's yes, Jesus's hidden years and his first sermon all happened in Nazareth.
places.scene: Nazareth's hills and the great cone-shaped basilica dome at morning.
places.realVisit: Nazareth is two hours north of Jerusalem by bus; the basilica and St Joseph's are side by side.

spots.name: First-century house under the Sisters of Nazareth convent
spots.scene: Wide view down into the excavated rock-cut rooms beneath the convent at midday, a shaft of light falling across the old stone floor, no people close, no faces, God only as light.

spots.name: Nebi Sa'in ridge lookout above Nazareth
spots.scene: Wide view from the high ridge above Nazareth at late afternoon, white houses spilling down the basin and the Jezreel Valley spread out in golden haze; no close faces.

spots.name: Mensa Christi Church, Nazareth
spots.scene: Wide view of the small Franciscan church tucked among old Nazareth houses at morning, the town spreading down the hillside behind, no close faces.

spots.name: Mount Precipice
spots.scene: A cliff edge over the Jezreel Valley at sunset, a crowd far behind, a path leading away.

spots.name: Basilica of Jesus the Adolescent, Nazareth
spots.scene: Wide view of the Salesian basilica on the ridge at sunset with all of Nazareth spread below, no close faces, never the face of Jesus.

spots.name: Upper basilica of the Annunciation
spots.scene: A soaring concrete dome with images of Mary from many nations, distant, in soft light.

places.name: Ein Karem (second visit)
places.why: The hill town of John the Baptist's birth, where Zechariah's Benedictus was sung.
places.scene: A green valley village of stone houses and church towers west of Jerusalem at morning.
places.realVisit: Ein Karem is a short bus or taxi ride from central Jerusalem.

spots.name: Benedictus courtyard, Church of St John the Baptist
spots.scene: A courtyard of ceramic plaques in many languages at morning, a bell tower above.

spots.name: Ein Hanniya spring
spots.scene: A spring pool with old arches by a desert road at noon, a chariot halted far off.

spots.name: Monastery of St John in the Wilderness (Even Sapir)
spots.scene: Wide view of the small monastery clinging to a terraced hillside west of Ein Karem at dawn, a spring-fed cave below and pines on the slopes; no close faces.

places.name: Church of the Nativity, Bethlehem
places.why: Bethlehem, where Christ was born, the Innocents mourned and Christmas is kept at midnight.
places.scene: Manger Square and the fortress-like Church of the Nativity at night, lamps glowing.
places.realVisit: Bethlehem is 20 minutes from Jerusalem by bus; enter the basilica through the low Door of Humility.

spots.name: Star Street, the old pilgrim way into Bethlehem
spots.scene: Wide view down the narrow stone lane of Star Street at dusk, lanterns strung overhead and the church bell tower beyond, a few distant walkers, no close faces.

spots.name: Grotto of the Nativity, silver star
spots.scene: A silver star in a marble floor ringed by hanging lamps at midnight.

spots.name: Church of St Catherine (Midnight Mass)
spots.scene: The Franciscan church full of candlelight on Christmas morning, organ pipes gleaming.

spots.name: Grotto of the Holy Innocents
spots.scene: A small dim rock chapel with a single candle, quiet and mourning.

spots.name: Grotto of St Jerome
spots.scene: A rock cave room by lamplight, a writing ledge, quiet.

spots.name: Cloister of St Catherine's Church, Jerome statue
spots.scene: A cloister with a statue of Jerome on a column at morning.

spots.name: Tombs of Paula and Eustochium
spots.scene: A small grotto chamber with two carved tombs and candles.

spots.name: Mar Saba Monastery
spots.scene: A monastery clinging to the Kidron gorge cliffs at sunrise.

spots.name: Shepherds' Field chapel, Beit Sahour
spots.scene: A tent-shaped chapel among olive trees on the Shepherds' Field at night, stars thick above.

spots.name: Church of St. Nicholas, Beit Jala
spots.scene: Wide view of the hilltop church of St. Nicholas in Beit Jala at winter dusk, lights strung over the old town, no close faces.

places.name: Sea of Galilee shore at Magdala (second visit)
places.why: Magdala, home of Mary Magdalene, and the lake where Peter fell at Jesus' knees.
places.scene: The Sea of Galilee at Magdala at morning, cliffs of Arbel behind.
places.realVisit: Magdala is on the lake road north of Tiberias; the Jesus Boat is at Kibbutz Ginosar nearby.

spots.name: Tiberias old harbor where fishing boats moor
spots.scene: Wide view of the Tiberias harbor at first light, small fishing boats tied along the black basalt quay and nets drying, the still lake stretching to the Golan hills; no close faces.

spots.name: Excavated first-century market street of Magdala
spots.scene: Wide view along the excavated paving stones of the Magdala market street at golden hour, low walls and shop doorways leading toward the lake, no close faces.

spots.name: First-century mikvaot (ritual baths) of Magdala
spots.scene: Wide view of the excavated stone ritual baths of Magdala in soft morning light, groundwater glinting in the steps and the lake beyond the palms; no close faces.

spots.name: Magdala lakeshore pier
spots.scene: A wooden pier at dawn, a woman walking along the shore far off.

places.name: Mount of Beatitudes (second visit)
places.why: The hillside of the Sermon on the Mount, which Luke sets on a plain.
places.scene: Gardens and an octagonal church above the Sea of Galilee at morning.
places.realVisit: The Mount of Beatitudes is above Tabgha; a footpath leads down to the lake.

spots.name: Gennesaret plain fields below the hills
spots.scene: Wide view across the flat green fields of the Gennesaret plain in early morning, the hills rising behind and the lake glinting to the east, a few distant figures, no close faces.

spots.name: Hillside path below the Beatitudes
spots.scene: A path through banana groves down to the water at evening light.

places.name: Church of the Multiplication, Tabgha (second visit)
places.why: Near Tabgha and Bethsaida the crowds were fed, and the risen Jesus cooked fish on the shore.
places.scene: Tabgha's lakeshore of springs and churches at morning.
places.realVisit: Tabgha lies on the north shore between Capernaum and Ginosar; Bethsaida is a short drive east.

spots.name: Beteiha plain on the north-east shore
spots.scene: Wide view over the grassy Beteiha plain in late afternoon, the lake shimmering beyond and the Golan slopes behind, an empty road, no faces.

spots.name: Heptapegon shoreline (charcoal fire tradition)
spots.scene: A small charcoal fire on flat rocks by the lake at dawn, a net drying.

places.name: Mount Arbel and the Galilee fields
places.why: The fields, trails and synagogues of the Galilee where Jesus taught as he walked.
places.scene: Arbel's cliffs above the green Galilee valleys and the lake at morning.
places.realVisit: Arbel National Park is west of the lake; the Jesus Trail passes through it on foot.

spots.name: Arbel summit lookout
spots.scene: The cliff edge at dawn looking down on the lake, a road leading south.

spots.name: Jesus Trail through the Arbel valley
spots.scene: A footpath through a green valley at morning, small groups walking in pairs.

spots.name: Arbel ancient synagogue
spots.scene: A ruined synagogue facing Jerusalem at evening, columns catching the light.

spots.name: Wadi Hamam fields
spots.scene: Village fields at noon, a crowd gathered and a woman's voice rising.

spots.name: Ginosar valley grain fields
spots.scene: Full grain fields at harvest, a big new barn on the edge, evening sky.

spots.name: Wildflower slopes of the Horns of Hattin
spots.scene: Red anemones across a hillside in spring sun, birds overhead.

places.name: Mount of Olives (second visit)
places.why: From Bethphage to Bethany, the Mount of Olives holds Jesus' tears, Lazarus and the Ascension.
places.scene: The Mount of Olives at golden hour, churches and olive trees above the Old City.
places.realVisit: Walk up from the Kidron Valley or take a taxi to the top and walk down the Palm Sunday road.

spots.name: Fig orchards on the eastern slope
spots.scene: A fig tree without fruit beside a terrace at morning, a gardener with a spade.

spots.name: Augusta Victoria Hospital church
spots.scene: A hospital and bell tower on the ridge at afternoon, someone walking upright through the gate.

spots.name: Dominus Flevit (hen mosaic)
spots.scene: A teardrop-shaped chapel with a mosaic of a hen and chicks at morning.

spots.name: Tomb of the Prophets Haggai and Malachi, Mount of Olives
spots.scene: Wide view from the ancient burial cave's entrance at sunset, the walls and golden dome of Jerusalem spread across the valley, no close faces.

spots.name: Ridge path toward Bethany
spots.scene: A ridge path at dawn, a small group walking with hands lifted.

spots.name: Bethany hillside above the Jericho road
spots.scene: Wide view from the Bethany hillside at late afternoon, the old road dropping east toward the desert and the town's roofs below, no close faces.

spots.name: Old Roman road climbing from the Jericho desert to Bethany
spots.scene: Wide view of the old road climbing out of the desert toward Bethany at dusk, worn paving and bare hills turning rose, a distant figure walking up toward the village; no close faces.

spots.name: Jewish cemetery hillside
spots.scene: Thousands of stone graves on the slope at sunrise, a grain field behind the wall.

spots.name: Russian Ascension bell tower
spots.scene: A tall bell tower at the hilltop at noon, the horizon stretching to the edges of the earth.

spots.name: At-Tur village street on the Mount of Olives summit
spots.scene: Wide view down the narrow summit street of at-Tur on a bright spring morning, palm branches raised by a distant procession and the Old City walls glowing beyond; no close faces.

spots.name: Viri Galilaei estate, Mount of Olives
spots.scene: Wide view of the Greek Orthodox Viri Galilaei grounds at the north summit at noon, sky wide and bright overhead, no close faces, God only as light.

places.name: Capernaum (second visit)
places.why: Peter's town and Jesus' home base, where he spoke of the bread of life.
places.scene: Capernaum's black basalt ruins and white synagogue by the lake at morning.
places.realVisit: Capernaum is on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee, open daily with a small entry fee.

spots.name: Basalt house quarter (insula)
spots.scene: Low black-stone walls of village homes at noon, a long table imagined in a courtyard.

spots.name: Capernaum lakeside gate
spots.scene: A gate opening to the shore at evening, a road busy with people coming in.

spots.name: Church of the Seven Apostles (red domes)
spots.scene: Pink domes by the shore at sunrise, the water perfectly still.

spots.name: Carved lintels with the manna jar, Capernaum
spots.scene: Wide view of the carved limestone friezes laid out beside the synagogue in morning sun, the lake beyond, no close faces.

spots.name: Dalmanutha open-air lakeside altar, Tabgha
spots.scene: Wide view of the simple open-air stone altar under trees by the water at Tabgha at sunrise, rows of benches facing the lake and light spreading over the water; no close faces.

spots.name: Lakeshore path from Capernaum to Tabgha
spots.scene: Wide view along the shoreline path between Capernaum and Tabgha in early evening, black basalt stones, eucalyptus shade and a few distant walkers turning toward the town; no close faces.

places.name: Jericho oasis (second visit)
places.why: Jericho's palaces, springs and sycamores frame Jesus' parables of money, prayer and Zacchaeus.
places.scene: The palm oasis of Jericho below desert cliffs at golden hour.
places.realVisit: Jericho is 40 minutes from Jerusalem; a cable car climbs to the Mount of Temptation.

spots.name: Herod's winter palaces (Tulul Abu el-Alayiq)
spots.scene: Ruined palace walls by a dry wadi at morning, a steward walking with ledgers.

spots.name: Hisham's Palace gate
spots.scene: A grand carved gateway at dusk, a poor man lying at the threshold, dogs nearby.

spots.name: Elisha's Spring (Ein es-Sultan)
spots.scene: A spring flowing among palms at noon, a woman walking on toward the town.

spots.name: St George's Monastery, Wadi Qelt
spots.scene: A monastery clinging to a cliff in a desert gorge at morning, one figure praying below.

spots.name: Zacchaeus sycamore tree
spots.scene: An ancient sycamore in a fenced garden at afternoon, a small figure in its branches.

places.name: The Cenacle (Upper Room), Mount Zion
places.why: The Upper Room: the Last Supper, the washing of feet, the gift of the Spirit and the first Church.
places.scene: Mount Zion at evening, the Dormition Abbey tower and the Cenacle's stone roofs.
places.realVisit: The Cenacle is on Mount Zion just outside Zion Gate, open daily; the Dormition Abbey is next door.

spots.name: Upper Room Gothic hall
spots.scene: An empty vaulted hall at evening, warm light through high windows.

spots.name: Tomb of David hall below the Cenacle
spots.scene: Wide view of the vaulted stone hall beneath the Cenacle in quiet morning light, a draped cenotaph far down the room, no close faces.

spots.name: Lower hall beneath the Upper Room
spots.scene: A low stone room at night with a basin of water and a towel on the floor.

spots.name: Pelican capital, Upper Room
spots.scene: A carved column capital showing a pelican feeding its young, lit by a sunbeam.

spots.name: Sleeping Mary statue, Hagia Maria Sion crypt
spots.scene: Wide view of the round crypt in candlelight, the reclining statue of Mary small at the centre beneath a mosaic dome, no close faces.

spots.name: Armenian Church of St Saviour, Mount Zion
spots.scene: Wide view of the Armenian courtyard and church walls on Mount Zion at evening, olive trees and old stone in calm light, no close faces.

spots.name: Stairway to the Holy Spirit chapel
spots.scene: A stone stair rising toward a shut door at night, a soft glow behind it.

spots.name: Apse and zodiac floor of Hagia Maria Sion
spots.scene: Wide view across the circular church's mosaic floor of zodiac and apostles' names in midday light, the golden apse far ahead, no close faces.

spots.name: Upper Room windows at morning
spots.scene: Morning sun bursting through the Gothic windows like tongues of fire.

spots.name: Ararat Street gateway by the Syriac Convent
spots.scene: Wide view down the narrow Ararat Street at night, a heavy door in the stone wall lit by a single lamp, no people close, no faces.

spots.name: Armenian Cathedral of St James
spots.scene: A dim cathedral hung with lamps, elders seated around the walls.

spots.name: Bell tower of Hagia Maria Sion
spots.scene: Wide view of the tall bell tower and conical dome over Mount Zion at Pentecost dawn, light spilling across the old stone, no close faces, God only as light.

spots.name: Rooftop terrace above the Cenacle
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Rooftop terrace above the Cenacle at windy afternoon: domes and bell towers of Mount Zion under moving clouds, a single shaft of light; no close faces.

spots.name: Rooftop terrace over the Cenacle
spots.scene: A flat stone rooftop at dusk, the domes and towers of Jerusalem spread out beneath an apricot sky.

spots.name: Armenian Patriarchate Road, Mount Zion
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Armenian Patriarchate Road, Mount Zion at weekday morning: a narrow stone lane where shopkeepers, students and priests pass each other at a distance; no close faces.

spots.name: Hinnom Valley path below Mount Zion
spots.scene: Wide view up the Hinnom Valley path at dusk, the abbey's conical roof on the ridge above, no close faces.

spots.name: St. Saviour's Monastery, Jerusalem
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of St. Saviour's Monastery, Jerusalem at evening: the Franciscan parish church's bell tower over the Christian Quarter; no close faces.

spots.name: Hurva Synagogue square, Jewish Quarter
spots.scene: Wide view of Hurva Square at early morning, the white dome above the stone plaza where pilgrims from many nations once crowded at the feast, no close faces.

places.name: Garden of Gethsemane, Mount of Olives (second visit)
places.why: Jesus prayed in agony and was arrested in Gethsemane; Mary's tomb lies close by.
places.scene: Ancient olive trees and the Church of All Nations at the foot of the Mount of Olives at night.
places.realVisit: Gethsemane is at the bottom of the Mount of Olives, across the Kidron from the Lions' Gate.

spots.name: Church of All Nations façade at night
spots.scene: Wide view of the church façade from the road at night, its columns and gold mosaic softly floodlit and distant, olive trees black in the foreground, no close faces, never the face of Jesus, God only as light.

spots.name: Kidron Valley floor below the Golden Gate
spots.scene: Wide view along the dark Kidron Valley floor at night, torchlight far up the slope and the sealed Golden Gate above under a cold moon; no close faces.

spots.name: Ancient olive trees of the garden
spots.scene: Gnarled olive trunks at night, torches approaching between the trees.

spots.name: Tomb of the Virgin Mary
spots.scene: A deep staircase into a dark church hung with lamps, distant and still.

places.name: Via Dolorosa (second visit)
places.why: From Herod's palace to the Antonia fortress, the trial and the way of the cross.
places.scene: The Via Dolorosa's stone arches and market lanes at early morning.
places.realVisit: Walk the Via Dolorosa from the Lions' Gate; Franciscans lead the stations every Friday afternoon.

spots.name: Tower of David citadel (Herod's palace)
spots.scene: Citadel walls at morning, a crowd mocking at a distance, a royal robe on a stone.

spots.name: Eighth Station, Via Dolorosa
spots.scene: A small cross carved in a wall on a narrow lane, women weeping far off.

spots.name: Lithostrotos pavement, Sisters of Zion
spots.scene: Ancient paving stones under a vault, game scratches in the stone, dim light.

places.name: Patmos
places.why: John received the Apocalypse on Patmos; the letters of love were treasured there.

places.why: Laodicea, warned for being lukewarm, sat between Hierapolis' hot springs and Colossae's cold water.

places.why: The Ghent Altarpiece paints the Apocalypse's heavenly worship of the Lamb.

places.name: Solesmes Abbey (second visit)

places.realVisit: Solesmes is near Sablé-sur-Sarthe; visitors may join the monks for Mass and Vespers.

places.name: Cologne Cathedral (second visit)
places.why: The Shrine of the Three Kings makes Cologne the Magi's city.
places.scene: Cologne's twin spires over the Rhine at winter evening.
places.realVisit: Cologne Cathedral is next to the main train station, open daily.

places.why: The Pope begins Lent at Santa Sabina; the Aventine keeps Rome's Lenten station walks.

spots.name: Kalwaria Zebrzydowska calvary paths

places.why: Bethany, home of Martha, Mary and Lazarus.
places.scene: Olive slopes at dawn.
places.realVisit: Walk from Jerusalem Old City.

spots.scene: Wide view of the small Greek Orthodox chapel beside the old Jericho road at the edge of Bethany in late afternoon, stone walls warm in the sun; no close faces.

places.name: Budapest

places.realVisit: Fly or train to Budapest.

places.realVisit: Drive from Madaba.

places.realVisit: Drive from Rennes.

spots.scene: Motherhouse chapel at August morning.

places.why: The abbey of the archangel on the sea.

places.realVisit: Bus from Rennes.

places.realVisit: Train from Barcelona.

spots.scene: Church at October morning.

places.why: Albert the Great, scientist and saint.
places.scene: Cologne Cathedral and Rhine at dusk.
places.realVisit: Train to Köln Hbf.

spots.scene: Romanesque church at November morning.

places.name: St. Charles, Missouri
places.why: Philippine Duchesne.
places.scene: River town at evening.
places.realVisit: Drive from St Louis.

spots.scene: Shrine at November morning.

places.name: Via Dolorosa (third visit)
places.why: Mary's early life, remembered at St Anne's.
places.scene: Old City lane at dawn.
places.realVisit: Walk from Lions' Gate.

spots.name: St Anne's Church and Pool of Bethesda
spots.scene: Crusader church at November morning.

places.name: Mount Sinai and St. Catherine's Monastery (third visit)
places.why: Catherine of Alexandria.
places.scene: Monastery under the mountain at dawn.
places.realVisit: Bus from Sharm el-Sheikh.

spots.scene: Monastery at November dawn.

places.name: Basilica of St. Nicholas, Bari
places.why: Nicholas, the gift-giving bishop.
places.scene: Basilica by the sea at evening.
places.realVisit: Train from Rome or Naples.

spots.scene: Crypt with candles at December evening.

places.name: St. Peter's Square
places.why: Year four opens the Catechism at the square where the whole Church gathers.
places.scene: Bernini's colonnade opens like two arms around the oval square at early morning, the obelisk's shadow long across the cobbles.
places.realVisit: Free to walk in any day; Wednesday audiences and Sunday Angelus fill it with pilgrims.

spots.name: Fountain of the Four Rivers, Piazza Navona
spots.scene: Wide view of Piazza Navona at early morning, Bernini's four great river figures around the obelisk, the square still empty and gold, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide view down the double-helix Bramante Staircase at midday, light falling from the oculus, a few distant visitors spiralling, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide view of the Room of the Segnatura in afternoon light, the great frescoed walls of theology and philosophy facing each other, no close faces.

spots.name: Statue of St. Peter before the basilica steps
spots.scene: A distant stone statue of Peter holding the keys stands before the wide basilica steps under a clear noon sky.

spots.name: Cortile della Pigna, Vatican Museums
spots.scene: The great bronze pinecone sits in its niche above a long courtyard in afternoon light, library windows lining the walls.

places.name: İznik (ancient Nicaea)
places.why: The Creed was shaped at Nicaea, so the lessons on believing together are taught here.
places.scene: The small walled lake town of İznik at golden hour, red roofs and Roman walls beside a wide still lake.
places.realVisit: About two hours from Istanbul by ferry and road; the old town is walkable in a day.

spots.name: Beştaş Roman obelisk near İznik
spots.scene: Wide view of the lone Roman obelisk in the olive fields outside İznik at late afternoon, the lake glinting beyond, no close faces.

spots.name: Abdülvahap hill viewpoint over İznik
spots.scene: Wide view from Abdülvahap hill at sunset over the walled grid of İznik and its lake, the old city where the Creed was shaped, no close faces.

spots.name: Lake İznik shore at sunrise
spots.scene: Wide view of the lake at sunrise, the first light spreading across calm water toward far mountains.

spots.name: Submerged Basilica of St. Neophytos
spots.scene: The outline of an ancient basilica shows beneath clear shallow water near the shore in soft morning light.

places.name: Monte Sant'Angelo, Gargano
places.why: Europe's oldest shrine of the archangel Michael holds lessons on providence, angels and the human person.
places.scene: A white hill town on the Gargano ridge at morning, sea haze below and the shrine's octagonal bell tower rising above the roofs.
places.realVisit: Reachable by bus from Foggia or Manfredonia; the grotto is open daily.

spots.name: Foresta Umbra beech forest
spots.scene: Ancient beech trunks rise in green shade at mid-morning, shafts of light reaching the forest floor.

spots.name: Grotto of St. Michael the Archangel
spots.scene: Steps descend into a candlelit cave church, a distant statue of the archangel high on the rock wall.

spots.name: Baptistery of San Giovanni in Tumba
spots.scene: A small stone medieval tower stands in a quiet lane in late afternoon, its doorway half in shadow.

places.name: Basilica of the Annunciation, Nazareth (fourth visit)
places.why: The town of the hidden life is where the Creed's lessons on Christ's birth and ordinary years are taught.
places.scene: Nazareth's hillside streets at late afternoon, the lantern-shaped dome of the basilica above stone roofs.
places.realVisit: Nazareth is about 40 minutes from Haifa by bus; the basilica is free to enter.

spots.name: Courtyard of Marian mosaics, Nazareth
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Courtyard of Marian mosaics, Nazareth at bright morning: colonnaded walls lined with mosaics sent from nations around the world; no close faces.

spots.name: Centre International Marie de Nazareth
spots.scene: Wide view of the Marie de Nazareth centre's rooftop garden at morning, the Annunciation dome rising across the street, no close faces.

spots.name: Ancient bathhouse by Mary's Well, Nazareth
spots.scene: Wide view of the old stone vaulted bathhouse beside Mary's Well at midday, ordinary village life outside, no close faces.

spots.name: Nazareth Village carpentry workshop
spots.scene: A reconstructed first-century village with stone terraces and a carpenter's bench in warm midday light, olive trees beyond.

places.name: Via Dolorosa (fourth visit)
places.why: Jerusalem's way of the cross holds the lessons on Pilate, the descent to the dead and the friars who keep the holy places.
places.scene: Narrow stone lanes of the Old City at early morning, arches overhead and the station markers on the walls.
places.realVisit: Walk it any day; the Franciscans lead the Way of the Cross every Friday afternoon.

spots.name: Kishle excavations beside the citadel
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Kishle excavations beside the citadel at early morning: excavated walls of Herod's palace prison under an Ottoman police building; no close faces.

spots.name: Garden Tomb, north of Damascus Gate
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Garden Tomb, north of Damascus Gate at dawn: a quiet garden with an ancient rock-cut tomb, its stone door groove in shadow; no close faces.

spots.name: Casa Nova Franciscan pilgrim house, Jerusalem
spots.scene: Wide view of the Franciscan Casa Nova pilgrim house lane near the New Gate at evening, pilgrims distant in the lamplight, no close faces.

places.name: Mount of Olives (fourth visit)
places.why: From the ridge facing the city, the lessons on Christ's return, the way of prayer and pilgrimage look out over Jerusalem.
places.scene: The Mount of Olives at golden hour, terraced tombs and olive trees falling toward the golden-domed Old City.
places.realVisit: A short walk from the Lions' Gate; best visited early before the heat.

spots.name: Seven Arches lookout over the Old City
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Seven Arches lookout over the Old City at sunrise: the whole golden city spread out below the olive slopes, light breaking over the walls; no close faces.

spots.name: St. George's Anglican Cathedral, Jerusalem
spots.scene: Wide view of St. George's Cathedral and its cloister garden at late afternoon, the bell tower above East Jerusalem streets, no close faces.

spots.name: Russian Church of Mary Magdalene
spots.scene: Golden onion domes rise above dark cypresses on the hillside in morning light.

spots.name: Haas Promenade lookout over Jerusalem
spots.scene: Wide view from the Haas Promenade at sunset across the valley to the Old City and the Mount of Olives, no close faces.

spots.name: Mount Scopus lookout over the desert
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Mount Scopus lookout over the desert at dawn: bare desert hills rolling down toward the Dead Sea haze; no close faces.

spots.name: Tantur hilltop on the Bethlehem road
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Tantur hilltop on the Bethlehem road at afternoon: an ecumenical institute on a hill looking to both Jerusalem and Bethlehem; no close faces.

places.name: Solesmes Abbey
places.why: The abbey that revived Gregorian chant teaches what liturgy is and why song prays twice.
places.scene: The long grey abbey wall rising above the river Sarthe at dusk, lights on in the church windows.
places.realVisit: Solesmes is near Sablé-sur-Sarthe by train; Vespers are sung daily and open to all.

spots.name: Banks of the Sarthe below the abbey
spots.scene: Calm river water reflects the fortress-like abbey at sunset, a last light on the walls.

spots.name: Monks' choir of Solesmes at Vespers
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Monks' choir of Solesmes at Vespers at evening: rows of distant white-robed monks in the long choir, candlelight and chant filling the nave; no close faces.

spots.name: Notre-Dame church, Sablé-sur-Sarthe
spots.scene: Wide view of Sablé's Notre-Dame church above the Sarthe at Sunday morning, people distant on the bridge, no close faces.

spots.name: Abbey gardens and terraces of Saint-Pierre de Solesmes
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Abbey gardens and terraces of Saint-Pierre de Solesmes at spring morning: clipped gardens stepping down to the river beside the abbey walls; no close faces.

spots.name: Medieval frescoed church of Asnières-sur-Vègre
spots.scene: Wide view of the small Romanesque church at Asnières beside the Vègre at dusk, its painted walls glimpsed through the open door, no close faces.

places.name: Chartres Cathedral (fourth visit)
places.why: A cathedral built as a book in stone teaches sacred time and what each part of a church means.
places.scene: Chartres' two mismatched spires above the wheat fields of the Beauce at sunrise.
places.realVisit: An hour from Paris by train; the labyrinth is uncovered on Fridays in summer.

spots.name: Astronomical clock, Chartres Cathedral
spots.scene: An ornate Renaissance clock face in the dim ambulatory, a beam of colored light crossing it.

spots.name: Église Saint-Pierre, lower town of Chartres
spots.scene: Wide view of the abbey church of Saint-Pierre in Chartres' lower town at morning, altar, ambo and font visible down the long nave, no close faces.

places.name: Ravenna (third visit)
places.why: Ravenna's Byzantine mosaics show many rites in one faith and the old shape of baptism and anointing.
places.scene: Low brick churches in a quiet Italian city at early evening, their plain outsides hiding golden interiors.
places.realVisit: Ravenna is an hour from Bologna by train; one ticket covers most mosaic sites.

spots.name: Basilica of San Giovanni Evangelista, Ravenna
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Basilica of San Giovanni Evangelista, Ravenna at morning: a plain brick basilica with a squat bell tower near the old harbour road; no close faces.

spots.name: Ravenna Cathedral (Basilica Ursiana)
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Ravenna Cathedral (Basilica Ursiana) at midday: a pale baroque cathedral beside its ancient octagonal baptistery; no close faces.

spots.name: Pineta di Classe pine forest

places.why: Orvieto keeps the Eucharistic miracle of Bolsena and the hymns Thomas Aquinas wrote here for Corpus Christi.
places.scene: A hilltop town on a cliff of volcanic rock at sunset, the striped cathedral rising above the plain.
places.realVisit: A funicular climbs from Orvieto's train station; Rome is about an hour away.

spots.name: Rocca Albornoz gardens at the cliff edge

places.why: The village of the Curé of Ars, confessor to thousands, teaches conversion, penance, anointing and parish life.

spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Birth house of the Curé of Ars, Dardilly at overcast morning: a modest farmhouse and chapel in rolling fields outside Lyon; no close faces.

places.name: Porziuncola, Santa Maria degli Angeli
places.why: The little chapel at the heart of the Franciscan story teaches the Pardon of Assisi, the call to live the gospel and Francis's death.

places.realVisit: Santa Maria degli Angeli is beside Assisi's train station; open all day.

places.name: Basilica della Santa Casa, Loreto (second visit)
places.why: The house of the Holy Family teaches marriage, the domestic church and the Litany of Loreto.
places.scene: A fortified hilltop basilica above the Adriatic at evening, its green dome glowing in the last light.
places.realVisit: Loreto has a train station near Ancona; the basilica is open from early morning.

spots.scene: An arcaded square with a bronze fountain at sunset, pilgrims small beneath the arches.

places.name: Naples, historic center
places.why: Naples' street faith teaches sacramentals, popular piety and the dead, and keeps the crucifix that spoke to Aquinas.
places.scene: The dense old city of Naples at dusk, laundry lines over narrow streets and Vesuvius faint beyond the bay.
places.realVisit: Walk Spaccanapoli from the train station; churches open mornings and late afternoons.

spots.scene: A narrow lane of nativity-figure workshops lit at evening, tiny crafted figures crowding the stalls.

spots.name: Piazza San Domenico Maggiore
spots.scene: A baroque spire in a quiet piazza on a cold December morning, the church's apse behind.

places.name: Mount of Beatitudes (third visit)
places.why: The hill of the Beatitudes opens the lessons on the moral life and what makes an act good.
places.scene: A green hill above the blue Sea of Galilee at morning, an octagonal church among palms.
places.realVisit: A short drive from Tiberias; the gardens close at midday.

spots.name: Sisters' orchard on the Mount of Beatitudes
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Sisters' orchard on the Mount of Beatitudes at spring morning: palm and flower gardens sloping toward the bright Sea of Galilee; no close faces.

spots.name: Beatitudes hillside sloping to the lake

places.name: Oxford, the city of John Henry Newman (second visit)
places.why: Newman, the great teacher of conscience, preached and converted here, so conscience and virtue are taught in Oxford.
places.scene: Oxford's spires above college roofs in a soft grey morning, mist on the meadows.
places.realVisit: Oxford is an hour from London by train; Littlemore is a short bus ride.

spots.scene: Wide establishing view of St Mary and St Nicholas, Littlemore at grey morning: the small stone church Newman built, standing on a quiet village lane; no close faces.

spots.name: Blackfriars Hall, St Giles, Oxford
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Blackfriars Hall, St Giles, Oxford at autumn afternoon: a stone Dominican priory on a wide tree-lined street; no close faces.

spots.name: Oxford Oratory, Church of St. Aloysius
spots.scene: A Victorian church on a leafy street at Sunday evening, warm light through the doors.

spots.name: Trinity College gardens, Oxford
spots.scene: A wide lawn before old college buildings at golden hour, long shadows on the grass.

places.name: Siena (third visit)
places.why: Siena's civic frescoes and saints teach the common good, natural law and grace, and Catherine's lay Dominican life.
places.scene: The shell-shaped Piazza del Campo and the tall Torre del Mangia at golden hour.
places.realVisit: Siena is reached by bus from Florence in about 75 minutes; the old town is walkable.

spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Sala della Pace, Palazzo Pubblico, Siena at afternoon: the frescoed hall of good and bad government seen wall to wall; no close faces.
