spots.name: Piccolomini Library, Siena Cathedral
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Piccolomini Library, Siena Cathedral at morning: bright frescoed walls and open choir books in a glowing room; no close faces.

spots.name: Basilica of San Francesco, Siena
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Basilica of San Francesco, Siena at late morning: a vast brick friars' church on its own piazza at the city's edge; no close faces.

spots.name: Fontebranda fountain, Siena
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Fontebranda fountain, Siena at afternoon: a Gothic arched fountain in the dyers' quarter where Catherine grew up; no close faces.

places.name: Mount Sinai and St. Catherine's Monastery (fourth visit)
places.why: Where the commandments were given, the commandments and the Church's precepts are taught.
places.scene: Red granite peaks above St. Catherine's Monastery at dawn, the first light on the summit.
places.realVisit: Reached from Sharm el-Sheikh or Dahab; pilgrims climb at night for sunrise.

spots.name: St. Catherine's Monastery library
spots.scene: Thick fortress walls of the ancient monastery at morning, a small window where old books are kept.

spots.name: Wadi al-Arbain, Monastery of the Forty Martyrs
spots.scene: Wide view of the walled garden monastery in the valley of the Forty Martyrs at dawn, granite peaks all around, no close faces.

spots.name: Chapel of St. Catherine on Jebel Katarina
spots.scene: Wide view of the tiny summit chapel on Jebel Katarina at first light, ridges of Sinai fading into the distance, no close faces.

spots.name: Bedouin village of Saint Catherine (al-Milga)
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Bedouin village of Saint Catherine (al-Milga) at Friday evening: low houses and gardens at the foot of the granite mountains, quiet at day's end; no close faces.

spots.name: Charnel house in the monastery garden, St. Catherine's
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Charnel house in the monastery garden, St. Catherine's at late afternoon: a walled garden of olive and cypress trees below the monastery walls; no close faces.

spots.name: Tamarisk valley of Wadi el-Sheikh
spots.scene: Wide view of the broad Wadi el-Sheikh with its tamarisk groves at evening, camels resting far off, no close faces.

places.name: Rome along the Tiber
places.why: Rome's river quarter, with its hospital, market, mouth of truth and Sant'Egidio, teaches how faith shapes daily moral life.
places.scene: The Tiber curving under old bridges at golden hour, Tiber Island in midstream and church domes behind.
places.realVisit: All within walking distance in central Rome; Sant'Egidio welcomes visitors at evening prayer.

spots.name: Fatebenefratelli hospital, Tiber Island
spots.scene: A boat-shaped island in the river with its old hospital at morning, water rushing past the weir.

spots.name: Sant'Agnese in Agone, Piazza Navona
spots.scene: A baroque dome over a long piazza at dawn, fountains splashing and the square nearly empty.

spots.name: Porta Portese market
spots.scene: Long rows of Sunday market stalls by an old city gate at morning, crowds small and distant.

spots.name: Botanical Garden of Rome
spots.scene: Green paths and palms climbing the Janiculum slope in soft afternoon light.

spots.name: Bocca della Verità, Santa Maria in Cosmedin
spots.scene: The great stone mask in the church porch at noon, a tall Romanesque bell tower above.

spots.name: Mensa of Via Dandolo, Trastevere
spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Mensa of Via Dandolo, Trastevere at evening: a doorway on a sloping street where guests line up for a meal, all small and distant; no close faces.

spots.name: Sant'Egidio community, Piazza Sant'Egidio
spots.scene: A small Trastevere square at evening, people arriving for prayer under warm windows.

spots.name: Caritas hostel at Termini station
spots.scene: A plain shelter doorway near the station at night, a light on and a meal being served inside.

spots.name: Santissima Trinità dei Pellegrini
spots.scene: A quiet baroque church at Sunday morning, candles lit on a high altar far down the nave.

places.name: Camaldoli
places.why: The forest hermitage of Camaldoli teaches purity of heart, freedom from envy and what prayer is.
places.scene: A hermitage of small cells hidden in deep fir forest in the Tuscan mountains at early morning mist.
places.realVisit: Drive or bus from Arezzo or Florence; guests can stay at the monastery.

spots.name: Sacro Eremo of Camaldoli
spots.scene: Rows of little hermit cottages each with a walled garden among tall firs, morning mist drifting.

spots.name: Monastery of Camaldoli
spots.scene: A stone monastery and old pharmacy beside a mountain stream at noon.

spots.name: Casentino forest above the hermitage
spots.scene: Tall silver firs and filtered light on a quiet path at late afternoon.

places.name: Mount Carmel, Haifa (second visit)
places.why: Elijah's mountain, birthplace of the Carmelites, teaches Old Testament prayer, the Carmelite rule and Mary of Carmel.
places.scene: The Carmel ridge above Haifa Bay at sunset, a monastery dome near the cliff edge and the sea below.
places.realVisit: Haifa's cable car climbs to Stella Maris; Muhraqa is a short drive along the ridge.

spots.name: Muhraqa, Carmelite monastery of the sacrifice of Elijah
spots.scene: A small stone monastery on a ridge top at morning, the Jezreel Valley spread far below.

spots.name: Wadi es-Siah, ruins of the first Carmelite hermitage

places.name: Garden of Gethsemane, Mount of Olives (third visit)
places.why: In the garden where Jesus prayed, the lessons on how he and his mother prayed are taught.
places.scene: Ancient olive trees in a walled garden at dusk, a mosaic church front behind them.
places.realVisit: At the foot of the Mount of Olives, a short walk from the Lions' Gate; open mornings and afternoons.

spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Franciscan prayer garden across from Gethsemane at night: olive terraces and small grottoes for prayer, lamps glowing among the trees; no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide establishing view of Church of Our Lady of the Ark of the Covenant, Abu Ghosh at morning: a hilltop church crowned by a statue of Mary holding the child, seen from afar; no close faces.

places.name: Church of the Pater Noster (Eleona)
places.why: The church where tradition places the teaching of the Our Father holds the lessons on the prayer itself.
places.scene: A cloister lined with tiled panels of the Our Father in many languages, cypress trees at golden hour.
places.realVisit: On the Mount of Olives summit, open mornings and afternoons except Sundays.

places.name: Roccasecca and Monte San Giovanni Campano
places.why: Thomas Aquinas's home country, where his family locked him in a tower, opens the Aquinas lessons.
places.scene: A ruined castle on a rocky hill above the Liri valley at morning, olive groves below.
places.realVisit: Near Frosinone in southern Lazio; reachable by car or regional train to Roccasecca.

places.name: Basilica of Santa Sabina, Aventine Hill (second visit)
places.why: Thomas began the Summa at the Dominican house on the Aventine, so its first arguments are taught here.
places.scene: An ancient basilica on the quiet Aventine hill at golden hour, orange trees and Rome's domes beyond.
places.realVisit: A short walk up the Aventine from Circo Massimo; the orange garden is free.

spots.scene: Wide morning view of the small round marble temple by the Tiber below the Aventine, its columns catching low gold light, a few distant walkers on the lawn, no close faces.

places.why: Medieval Paris, where Aquinas and Bonaventure taught, holds lessons on God, creation and the Church's teachers and seekers.
places.scene: Paris' Left Bank rooftops at early morning, the Panthéon dome and old college towers in grey light.
places.realVisit: All on foot in central Paris; the Sorbonne area is a short walk from Notre-Dame.

places.why: Cologne, where Thomas studied under Albert the Great, teaches happiness, habits and the cardinal virtues.

places.why: In Benedict's hometown, prayer and work, reading, hospitality and care of the sick are taught.

places.name: Abbey of Our Lady of Gethsemani
places.why: Thomas Merton's Trappist abbey shows how laypeople carry the Rule into ordinary days.

places.realVisit: Near Bardstown, Kentucky; the church and retreat house welcome visitors.

places.why: Assisi's hermitages, tombs and squares hold the stories of Francis, Clare and a church at peace with other faiths.

spots.scene: Open Umbrian fields with a small roadside shrine at sunrise, flocks of birds wheeling over the oaks.

places.name: Toulouse

places.name: Santo Domingo, Colonial Zone (second visit)
places.why: On Hispaniola a Dominican friar first preached against the colonists' cruelty: are these not men?

places.why: Rose of Lima and Martin de Porres, both Dominicans, lived their saintliness in this city.

places.name: Seville (second visit)
places.why: Seville faces its past honestly at the Inquisition's old castle and keeps faith in the streets in Holy Week.
places.scene: Seville's cathedral and Giralda tower above orange trees and white streets at golden hour.

places.name: Turin (second visit)
places.why: Turin, home of Pier Giorgio Frassati and Don Bosco's workers, teaches lay Dominican life and the dignity of labor.
places.scene: Turin's arcaded streets and baroque domes beneath the snowy Alps at morning.
places.realVisit: Turin has major train links; all sites are reachable by tram.

spots.name: Don Bosco's Valdocco Oratory
spots.scene: A busy courtyard with young people at afternoon, a basilica dome behind.

places.name: Convent of San Marco, Florence

places.scene: Florence's terracotta rooftops and the cathedral dome at sunrise.

places.name: Church of the Gesù, Rome

places.name: Souk Ahras (ancient Thagaste)
places.why: Augustine was born here, so his Confessions are first read in his own hill town.
places.scene: Wide view of a green Numidian hill town at early morning, olive groves on the slopes, soft light over red roofs.
places.realVisit: Fly to Annaba or Constantine, then drive about two hours inland to Souk Ahras.

places.name: Madauros (M'Daourouch) Roman ruins
places.why: Augustine went to school in Madauros and stole pears with friends back home: a youth among ruins.

places.realVisit: Drive about 25 km south of Souk Ahras to the M'Daourouch archaeological site.

places.name: Carthage (second visit)

places.scene: Wide view of Carthage hill and the blue Gulf of Tunis at golden hour, ruins scattered among pines.
places.realVisit: Take the TGM light rail from Tunis to the Carthage stops and walk between the sites.

places.scene: Wide view of Thonon above Lake Geneva at early morning, Swiss mountains across the water.
places.realVisit: Take the train to Thonon-les-Bains; the basilica and lake promenade are in the centre.

spots.scene: A basilica square at Lenten dusk, purple banners on balconies.

spots.scene: Wide view of the Plaza del Salvador and its church at Easter evening, orange trees and lamplight, no close faces.

spots.scene: The iron bridge at Pentecost sunset, the river red and wind in the flags.

places.name: Basilica of Mariazell
places.why: Austria's great pilgrimage town shows summer, harvest thanksgiving and November remembrance.
places.scene: Wide view of the basilica's three towers above the alpine town at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take the Mariazellerbahn narrow-gauge train from St. Pölten.

spots.name: Erlaufsee lake
spots.scene: A calm alpine lake on a summer morning, swimmers far off.

spots.scene: Red grave candles glowing at November dusk.

places.name: Naples Cathedral
places.why: Naples keeps feasts with food, saints and family; birthdays, name days and baptism days are learned here.
places.scene: Wide view of the cathedral and old Naples at morning.
places.realVisit: Take the Naples metro to Museo or Duomo station.

spots.name: Spaccanapoli
spots.scene: A long narrow street at afternoon, laundry and a birthday balloon far off.

spots.name: Santa Chiara majolica cloister
spots.scene: Painted tile benches under lemon trees at morning.

spots.scene: An ancient baptistery dome of blue-and-gold mosaics at noon.

spots.scene: Wide view of an ancient columned basilica inside the cathedral at quiet morning, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide view of a busy fish market under a medieval gate at early morning, baskets of silver fish on ice, no close faces.

places.name: Segovia, resting place of St. John of the Cross
places.why: John of the Cross is buried here; loss, failure, doubt and the dark night are walked through.
places.scene: Wide view of Segovia on its rock with the cathedral at sunset.
places.realVisit: Take the high-speed train from Madrid to Segovia (about 30 minutes).

spots.name: Segovia Cathedral
spots.scene: A Gothic cathedral at grey morning, one small candle lit in a side chapel.

spots.scene: Wide view of a sanctuary beneath a towering rock cliff at dark night, one lamp lit at the door, no close faces.

spots.scene: A hillside garden at night, a star-filled sky over the city walls.

places.name: Lampedusa (second visit)
places.why: Pope Francis's first trip was here; anger, wounds and a field-hospital Church meet at the sea.
places.scene: Wide view of the island's harbour at early morning.
places.realVisit: Fly or take the ferry from Sicily to Lampedusa.

spots.name: Isola dei Conigli beach
spots.scene: A turquoise cove under bare cliffs at stormy dusk.

spots.scene: Wide view of the small white sanctuary of Porto Salvo in its rocky valley at morning, the sea beyond, no close faces.

places.name: Capuchin Crypt, Rome
places.why: The friars' bone chapels say "what you are, we once were"; preparing for death is learned here.
places.scene: Wide view of Santa Maria della Concezione's stairs on Via Veneto at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take Rome metro line A to Barberini.

spots.name: Capuchin Crypt
spots.scene: Small vaulted chapels decorated with bones at morning, quiet and calm.

places.name: San Lorenzo fuori le Mura and Campo Verano
places.why: Rome's great cemetery and the basilica of the martyr Lawrence teach accompanying, funerals and grief.
places.scene: Wide view of the basilica and the cemetery gate at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take tram 19 or 3 in Rome to the Verano stop.

places.name: Appian Way and the catacombs
places.why: Early Christians buried their dead here in hope of resurrection.
places.scene: Wide view of the old Roman road lined with cypresses at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take bus 118 from central Rome to the Appia Antica park.

places.name: San Giovanni Rotondo, shrine of Padre Pio (second visit)
places.why: Padre Pio bore wounds and built a hospital called the Home for the Relief of Suffering.
places.scene: Wide view of the shrine and hospital on the Gargano hills at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take a bus from Foggia to San Giovanni Rotondo.

places.name: Sant'Egidio, Trastevere
places.why: The Community of Sant'Egidio prays and serves in Trastevere; service, study and community are learned here.
places.scene: Wide view of Trastevere's lanes and Santa Maria's bell tower at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take tram 8 from central Rome to Trastevere.

spots.scene: Wide view of a Trastevere street doorway at lunchtime, a queue and volunteers setting tables inside, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide view of a quiet medieval cloister with a well at Friday morning, no close faces.

places.name: Valdocco, Turin
places.why: Don Bosco's oratory mixed play, prayer and generosity for street boys.
places.scene: Wide view of the Basilica of Mary Help of Christians at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take a tram or bus in Turin to Valdocco.

spots.scene: A quiet courtyard of a charity house at morning.

spots.scene: Wide view of a baroque Marian sanctuary with its bell tower at early evening, no close faces.

places.why: Turin's seasons and its cathedral close the rule of life.
places.scene: Wide view of Turin with the Alps behind at early morning.
places.realVisit: Walk from Turin's Porta Nuova station.

spots.name: Basilica of Superga
spots.scene: A hilltop basilica at autumn morning, the Alps clear.

spots.name: Church of San Lorenzo, Piazza Castello
spots.scene: Wide view of a domed baroque church at a grand square at morning, no close faces.

places.name: Shrine of Our Lady of the Rosary, Pompeii (second visit)
places.why: Bartolo Longo built this rosary shrine beside the ruins; the first prayers are revisited here.
places.scene: Wide view of the shrine's bell tower with Vesuvius behind at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take the Circumvesuviana train from Naples to Pompei Santuario.

spots.scene: Wide view of the Great Theatre of Pompeii at evening, empty stone tiers under Vesuvius, no close faces.

places.name: St. Mark's Basilica, Venice
places.why: St. Mark's body rests here; his Gospel is reread under its golden domes.
places.scene: Wide view of the golden basilica on St. Mark's Square at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take the vaporetto to San Marco.

spots.scene: Golden domes at morning, light pouring from windows.

places.name: Abbey of Our Lady of Gethsemani (second visit)
places.why: Thomas Merton lived and wrote here.
places.scene: Wide view of the white abbey in Kentucky hills at early morning.
places.realVisit: Drive about an hour south of Louisville, Kentucky.

spots.name: Gethsemani welcome center and Merton exhibit
spots.scene: Wide view of a quiet visitor center among Kentucky trees at early autumn morning, no close faces.

places.name: Mount Sinai and St. Catherine's Monastery (fifth visit)
places.why: Genesis and Exodus are reread at the mountain of the covenant.
places.scene: Wide view of the granite mountains and the walled monastery at dawn.
places.realVisit: Travel from Sharm el-Sheikh to St. Catherine's; the summit climb starts at night.

spots.scene: Wide view of a walled green garden of olives and cypress below granite peaks at dawn, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide view from a low desert hill across the wide plain to Mount Sinai at golden morning, no close faces.

places.name: Ein Karem (fourth visit)
places.why: John the Baptist, the last prophet, was born here, and Luke tells of Mary's visit.
places.scene: Wide view of the green village and churches on terraced hills at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take a bus from central Jerusalem to Ein Karem.

spots.scene: Wide midday view of the small synagogue with its twelve jewel-colored windows blazing in the sun, light pooling in color across the floor, empty benches, no close faces.

spots.name: Notre-Dame de Sion convent, Ein Karem
spots.scene: Wide view of a convent garden of terraced paths and cypresses in Ein Karem at soft morning, no close faces.

places.name: Ephesus and the House of the Virgin Mary (fifth visit)
places.why: John, Paul and the Acts story all passed through Ephesus; John's Gospel, Acts, Paul and the Apocalypse are reread here.
places.scene: Wide view of the white marble ruins of Ephesus in a valley of olive trees at early morning.
places.realVisit: Fly to İzmir and drive about an hour south to Selçuk; the ruins and Mary's House are close by.

spots.name: Vineyards above Şirince
spots.scene: Wide view of terraced vineyards above the village of Şirince at harvest morning, no close faces.

spots.name: Commercial Agora (Tetragonos Agora), Ephesus
spots.scene: Wide view of a great square marketplace of ruined columns at bright morning, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide view of a hillside cave entrance above the ruined city at late afternoon, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide dawn view of the rock-cut catacomb church on the slope of Mount Pion, first light spilling into the old tomb openings, olive trees and a distant path, no figures close by.

places.name: İznik (ancient Nicaea)
places.why: The Council of Nicaea wrote the Creed and settled the date of Easter here; feasts, Fathers and councils are reviewed.
places.scene: Wide view of İznik's old walls beside a broad lake at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take a bus from Istanbul or Bursa to İznik.

spots.scene: Wide view of low Byzantine church foundations among trees at quiet morning, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide view of a domed Ottoman building with ancient stones in its garden at warm afternoon, no close faces.

spots.name: Yenişehir Gate, İznik walls
spots.scene: Wide view of a massive ancient city gate in the walls at golden evening, no close faces.

places.name: Trento Cathedral (second visit)
places.why: The Council of Trent met here; medieval saints, reform and modern saints are reviewed in the reform city.
places.scene: Wide view of Trento's cathedral square under green Alpine slopes at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take the train to Trento on the Verona–Brennero line.

spots.name: Palazzo Geremia, Trento
spots.scene: Wide view of a frescoed Renaissance palace on a Trento street at soft afternoon, no close faces.

spots.name: Doss Trento hill
spots.scene: Wide view from a wooded hilltop over the city and Alps at clear dusk, no close faces.

places.name: Santa Maria sopra Minerva, Rome
places.why: Dominicans kept Aquinas's teaching at the Minerva; the calendar and the Catechism are reviewed beside the Pantheon.
places.scene: Wide view of Bernini's elephant obelisk and the plain church front at early morning.
places.realVisit: Walk one minute from the Pantheon in central Rome.

spots.name: Santa Maria in Aquiro
spots.scene: Wide view of a baroque church facade on a small Roman piazza at morning, no close faces.

spots.name: Sant'Eustachio, Piazza Sant'Eustachio
spots.scene: Wide view of a small piazza with a church topped by a stag's head at early morning, no close faces.

spots.scene: Wide golden-hour view up the grand double staircase to the Baroque facade of Santi Domenico e Sisto, a few distant students on the steps, no close faces.

places.name: Church of the Gesù, Rome (second visit)
places.why: Rome holds a house of each great order: Benedict, Francis, Dominic, Ignatius and Carmel are reviewed in one walk.
places.scene: Wide view of the Gesù's Baroque façade on its busy square at early morning.
places.realVisit: Walk from Largo di Torre Argentina in central Rome; Ignatius's rooms are beside the church.

spots.scene: A tiny Romanesque church at morning, tradition marking Benedict's student room.

spots.name: Cordonata stairs to the Capitoline
spots.scene: Wide view up a long ramped stairway toward the Capitoline at sunrise, no close faces.

spots.name: Santa Sabina on the Aventine
spots.scene: A bright basilica and its orange garden at afternoon, Dominic's orange tree seen through a window.

spots.name: La Storta chapel, Via Cassia
spots.scene: Wide view of a small roadside chapel on an old road outside Rome at grey dawn, no close faces.

spots.name: Santa Maria della Vittoria
spots.scene: A Baroque chapel at night, a distant white marble Teresa in golden rays.

places.name: Hagia Sophia, Istanbul (fourth visit)
places.why: John XXIII, author of Pacem in Terris, served in Istanbul; social teaching, Mary and the Eastern Churches are reviewed in the city of Constantinople.
places.scene: Wide view of the great dome and minarets above the Bosphorus at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take the T1 tram to Sultanahmet in Istanbul.

spots.name: Cathedral of the Holy Spirit, Istanbul
spots.scene: A small cathedral courtyard at morning, a distant statue of John XXIII.

spots.name: Church of St. Mary of the Mongols
spots.scene: Wide view of a small red Byzantine church in a hillside Istanbul neighborhood at late afternoon, no close faces.

spots.name: Deësis mosaic, upper gallery of Hagia Sophia
spots.scene: Wide view along a marble gallery toward a distant golden mosaic panel at morning, sunlight slanting through windows, no close faces and no face of Jesus shown.

places.name: San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro, Pavia
places.why: Augustine's tomb lies here, closing the circle back to the Confessions.
places.scene: Wide view of the Romanesque church on a quiet Pavia street at early morning.
places.realVisit: Take the train from Milan to Pavia (about 30 minutes) and walk north.

spots.scene: A carved white marble shrine at morning, a golden apse shining behind it.

places.name: Mount of Beatitudes (fourth visit)
places.why: Faith, hope, charity and the Beatitudes are reviewed where the Sermon on the Mount was given.
places.scene: Wide view of the octagonal church and gardens above the blue Sea of Galilee at early morning.
places.realVisit: Drive or take a taxi about 15 km north of Tiberias.

spots.name: St. Peter's Church, Tiberias

spots.name: Korazim synagogue ruins
spots.scene: Wide view of black basalt ruins above the Sea of Galilee at warm morning, no close faces.
